Output: Climate financing platform to support new low-carbon technologies, MSEs, and ESCOs established Indicator: At least three new low-carbon technologies that have never been used commercially in Ningbo or the PRC piloted Progress/Status: Pre-due diligence and/or detailed due diligence reports have been prepared for at least three potential subprojects. Other potential new subprojects have been discussed during the inception mission in October 2024.
Potential subprojects with pre-DDR and/or detailed DDR: (i) Ningbo Chongtian New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.; (ii) Ningbo Yongneng Integrated Energy Service Co., Ltd.; and (iii) Cixi Water Investment Co., Ltd.
Potential subprojects discussed during the inception mission in October 2024 (i) Electric Battery Recycling and Circular Utilization Subproject; (ii) Synergistic Treatment and Circular Utilization Subproject for Slurry, Construction Debris, and Fly Ash; (iii) Ningbo Kitchen Waste Treatment Plant Phase II Technical Renovation and Expansion Subproject; and (iv) Solar Photovoltaic Hydrogen Corridor and Energy Storage Hydrogen Production Subproject.
Site visits have been conducted to subprojects (i) through (iii) in October 2024.
ADB has cleared three subprojects for retroactive financing: 1. Heshengda Industrial Waste Heat Utilization and Digital Energy Management System Subproject for CNY7.85 million. 2. Ninggang Waste Heat Utilization Subproject for CNY6.4 million. 3. Chongtian Distributed Rooftop Solar PV Subproject for CNY0.71 million.
The subprojects for 2025-2026 that are under due diligence or proposed for due diligence as discussed during the loan review mission in September 2025 are as follows:
1. Cixi Municipal Sold Waste Collection and Transportation (Phase 1) Subproject for CNY65 million. 2. Zhenhai Smart Municipal Solid Waste Sorting and Collection, Demonstration Subproject for CNY7.35 million. 3. Haochen Smart Cold-Chain Logistics Industrial Park and Supporting Facilities Subproject for CNY40 million. 4. Ningbo Waste Plastics Recycle Subproject for CNY45 million. 5. Ningbo Solar PV Hydrogen Corridor Renewable Subproject for CNY600 million.
The subloans approved by ADB in Q4 2025: 1. Ningbo Jinyao Machinery Company 1 MW Distributed Rooftop Solar PV Subproject with Ningbo Donghai Bank as the financial intermediary. 2. Construction of the Thermal Energy Comprehensive Utilization Project of Ningbo Aisikai Synthethic Rubber Co., Ltd., with Ningbo Commerce Bank as the financial intermediary. 3. Construction of the Heating Furnace Flue Gas Waste Heat Recovery Project of Ningbo Iron and Steel Co., Ltd., with Ningbo Commerce Bank as the financial intermediary. 4. Cixi Municipal Solid Waste Colection and Transportation Integration (Phase 1) Subproject, with Bank of Ningbo as the financial intermediary. 5. Zhenhai District Recyclable Materials Sorting Center Subproject, with Ningbo Commerce Bank as the financial intermediary. Data Source: Project reports (semiannual, annual), or records of NMG and the three financial intermediaries Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity in climate mitigation and green financing strengthened Indicator: At least 200 women entrepreneurs report increased understanding and knowledge of ESG through trainings organized by the project management office and Ningbo Women Entrepreneurs' Association Progress/Status: On 14 October 2024, IFS, ISSB Beijing Office, and IFRS Foundation Beijing Office provided training on green finance and transition finance for FIs, roadmap for development of green banks, introduction to IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and sustainability disclosure empowering enterprises to over 150 participants from enterprises, financial institutions, and government agencies on 14 October 2024, including 47 women, which accounted for 23.5% of the target number.
Data Source: List of attendees, survey of the participants Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity in climate mitigation and green financing strengthened Indicator: At least one corporate strategy or guideline for green transformation prepared for each financial intermediary Progress/Status: In October 2024, the Beijing Institute for Finance and Sustainability (IFS) engaged with three financial institutions (FIs) and established a timeline for developing a green transformation strategy or guideline.
In the loan review held in September 2025, IFS has been assisting each FI in formulating its corporate strategy for green transformation:
Bank of Ningbo is focused on strengthening its compliance with the Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) and advancing green project initiatives.
Ningbo Commerce Bank is working to enhance support for micro and small enterprises (MSEs) through the development of innovative financial products.
Ningbo Donghai Bank is prioritizing the expansion of its green finance capabilities and leadership within relevant departments.
All three institutions emphasized the critical need to integrate ESMS across their operations. Data Source: Annual reports of the three financial intermediaries Actual value:

Output: Digital carbon accounts for large industrial emitters established Indicator: A digital platform established with energy usage and carbon emissions data from major industrial emitters Progress/Status: No progress yet.
The following requirements for the digital carbon account platform were discussed during the inception mission in October 2024: (i) the NMG will ensure the implementing agencies and subborrowers, before the roll out the digital systems under the Project, (a) develop and implement data governance framework that adheres to nationally acceptable and where applicable, legally mandated, access, retention, disposal, cyber security, and information technology audit procedures for the information collected and managed in the information systems created, used and maintained under the Project; (b) undertake a study to detail out the risks including adherence to ethical principles in implementing information technology systems under the Project in matters related to automated processing and storage of individual information as applicable. The study should include development and implementation of transparent processes for ensuring collection, access, storage, dissemination and deletion of individual data, biometric data (if any), and or institutional information, development, and implementation of guidelines for ensuring adherence to intellectual property rights principles, processes preventing cyber bullying, and procedures for access to data / information from other law enforcing agencies; and (c) implement the measures and procedures recommended under the study referred to in subparagraph (b) above during the configuration and roll out of the information technology systems. Data Source: Project reports (quarterly, semiannual, annual) Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Target year: 2030 Target value: Established
